{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Ferdinand Joachimsthal.jpg|thumb|Ferdinand Joachimsthal]]

{{Use mdy dates|date=April 2016}}
'''Ferdinand Joachimsthal''' was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]].

He was born on March 9, 1818, at Goldberg ([[Złotoryja]]), [[Silesia]] and died on April 5, 1861, at [[Breslau]] (Wrocław). In the year of his graduation ([[Ph.D.]], [[Berlin]], 1842) he was appointed teacher at a ''[[Realschule]]'' in [[Berlin]], and in 1846 was admitted to the philosophical faculty of the university as ''[[privatdozent]]''. In 1856, he was appointed [[professor]] of mathematics at [[University of Halle|Halle]], and in 1858 at [[Breslau]].

Joachimsthal, who was [[Jewish]], contributed essays to ''[[Crelle's Journal]]'', 1846, 1850, 1854, 1861, and to [[Olry Terquem]]'s ''[[Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques]]''.

He is known for ''Joachimsthal's Equation''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/JoachimsthalsEquation.html|title=Joachimsthal's Equation}}</ref> and ''Joachimsthal Notation '',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cut-the-knot.org/Generalization/JoachimsthalsNotations.shtml|title = Joachimsthal's Notations}}</ref> both associated with [[conic section]]s.<ref>See "Conics and Joachimthal's equation" in [[Projective harmonic conjugate]]</ref>

== Works ==
* 1848: "Sur les normales infiniment voisines d'une surface courbe", [[Crelle's Journal]] 13: 415–22
* 1863: ''[https://archive.org/details/elementederanal00joacgoog/page/n10/mode/2up Elemente der analytischen Geometrie der Ebene]'' via [[Internet Archive]]
* 1872: ''[https://archive.org/details/anwendungderdif01joacgoog/page/n5/mode/2up Anwendung der Differential- und Integralrechnung]'' via Internet Archive
